Seizures / Convulsions
y
• Syncope
• Acute Dystonia
• Rigors
ABC
Left lateral 
position
Simple airway manoeuvres
Prep for Intubation
D E F G
1ml/kg 50% Dextrose
100mg Thiamine IM
Non-rebreather 
Facemask
Prep BMV + mask ±
OPA
IV or IO
Don’t try IV now
Use IM drugs
Check Sodium: < 115mmol/L = give 100mL 5% Saline
1st
Line
No IV
Midazolam 0,2mg/kg IMI (max 10mg IM)
IV insitu
Lorazepam 0,1mg/kg (max 8mg over 2 minutes) OR 
Clonazepam 0,02mg/kg (max 2mg over 30 sec)
Repeat benzo dose x1 after 5 minutes
Status Epilepticus (SE)
• Seizure > 5 min
• >2 Seizures w/o 
recovery to baseline
Consider toxicological causes* AND pregnancy with eclampsia!
2nd
Line
Valproate
20mg/kg IV at 5mg/kg/min (±5min)
Phenytoin
20mg/kg IV  at 50mg/min (±25min)
Repeat AED at ½ dose after 20 minutes
Don’t       Ever    Forget    Glucose!
*Omit 2nd line agents for toxin-induced seizures
Secure 
Airway
Pre-ox with BMV + PEEP valve
Sedative ± muscle relaxant
*Consider post-paralysis seizure monitoring
Don’t unnecessarily delay airway 
management for AED’s to take effect
Call for HELP
Ref: Dr J Hart. TMRH Protocols. Nov 2021 
Differential for 
convulsions
• Ventricular fibrillation
• Fasciculations
• Myoclonus
• Syncope
• Acute Dystonia
• Rigors
RMMCH EM Clinical Protocols V5 03/01/2024

Seizures / Convulsions 
Refractory SE: ongoing seizure 
activity despite adequately 
dosed 1st and 2nd line agents
Super-refractory SE: ongoing 
seizure activity for >24 hrs, OR 
despite 2 AEDs or 3rd
anaesthetic agents
3rd
Line
Propofol Infusion
1-4mg/kg/hr
Add adrenaline for vasodilation and hypotension
Midazolam Infusion
0,1mg/kg/hr
Choice agent for intractable hypotension
Ketofol Infusion
See TMRH  ED Protocol Guide
Phenobarbital
20mg/kg per NGT (IV not available at TMRH)
Delirium Tremens and super-refractory SE
Pyridoxine
5g per NGT
INH induced seizures and super-refractory SE
Post-intubation care
(FASTHUGS etc)
• Analgosedation
• Input/output (IV fluid + 
catheter)
• Lung-protective ventilation
Seizure Monitoring
(Esp. if paralysed)
• Continuous bedside EEG
• Unexplained sympathetic 
surge (↑HR, BP, mydriasis)
• Unexplained ↑lactate
ECG
Exclude dysrhythmia mimics
Signs of toxin (e.g. Na-channel blocker)
VBG
Electrolytes and glucose ±ventilation parameters
Bloods
FBC, UEC, CRP, CMP, Blood culture, HIV ±CD4
Known epileptic: add valp/phenyt/carbamaz level
Suspected ingestion/toxin:
- Add salicylate, carbamaz, phenyt, lithium, TCA (+paracet)
Imaging
CXR (post-intubation and CVC)
CT brain ±contrast
Other
Lumbar puncture ASAP
Investigations
Phenobarb 
may be considered 1st/2nd line in neonates / small infants 
 
 
Get from paediatrics (ward 17) if not avail in RMMCH ED
 
 
crush tablets with sterile water – administer down NGT
(IV not available at RMMCH)
RMMCH EM Clinical Protocols V5 03/01/2024
Ref: Dr J Hart. TMRH Protocols. Nov 2021 

Seizures / Convulsions
Back to baseline
• Check ECG, glucose
• Excl sepsis/meningitis, syncope, TIA/stroke, 
TRAUMA
• Send FBC, UEC, CRP
• Book outpatient contras
